name: Deglyph
pitch: Deglyph is a 2D action co-op game played on a grid-based world with smooth movement and combat. Players explore a vast world, enter user-created dungeons, battle monsters, and find epic loot in a peer-to-peer session; the world is built from coloured, shaped cells that combine into images, spaces, and UI.

decisions.question: For the monitor experience, should we treat 1920×1080 as the fixed logical game viewport and uniformly scale that view to other resolutions, so a 4K monitor shows the same amount of world at the same apparent size rather than more map?
decisions.answer: Yes—use 1920×1080 as both the default window resolution and fixed logical viewport; preserve the whole view with letterboxing on non-16:9 displays.
decisions.because: Higher pixel density should improve clarity without changing the apparent size of cells, interface elements, or the amount of world visible.
decisions.revisit_if: Playtesting shows the fixed view or letterboxing makes the game unreadable or materially harms use on a target display.
decisions.note: I want essentially the same game looking the same across all three of those resolutions, but the difference is the quality and the clarity.

decisions.question: What logical cell pitch should the fixed 1920×1080 viewport use so the visible grid is easy to scale across resolutions?
decisions.answer: Use 20 logical units per cell, giving a 96×54 visible-cell grid; maps remain free to be any width or height.
decisions.because: Twenty divides evenly into both logical viewport dimensions, while keeping the current map data independent from the amount of world visible on screen.
decisions.revisit_if: Playtesting shows 96×54 cells are too dense or too sparse for navigation, authoring, or readability.

decisions.question: How should Deglyph evaluate whether fullscreen cells are too large before changing the default view scale?
decisions.answer: Cycle the live cell pitches in the game with a debug key, reusing F3 rather than introducing another debug key.
decisions.because: The current fullscreen cells feel large, and direct comparison while moving through the world is more useful than choosing a scale from static examples.
decisions.revisit_if: The live comparison does not make the preferred fullscreen scale clear.
decisions.note: This settles how to evaluate the scale, not which pitch becomes the final default.

decisions.question: Which pitches should the live fullscreen-scale probe compare?
decisions.answer: Compare 12, 15, 20, 24, 30, and 60 logical units per cell.
decisions.because: These pitches divide the fixed 1920×1080 logical view and remain integer-sized when uniformly scaled to 1280×720, 640×360, 4K, and 8K, while covering substantially smaller and larger cells around the current reference.
decisions.revisit_if: A target display uses a different scale or the six live comparisons do not make the preferred fullscreen scale clear.
decisions.note: The 20-unit pitch is the current reference; this does not choose the final default.

decisions.question: Which debug key should temporarily cycle the fullscreen cell-scale probe without changing the existing performance overlay key?
decisions.answer: Use F4 for the temporary cell-scale experiment and leave F3 assigned to the performance overlay.
decisions.because: F3 is already the established performance overlay key, and a separate adjacent key keeps both debug tools understandable while the experiment is running.
decisions.revisit_if: The temporary probe is retained beyond the experiment or the debug-key layout is redesigned.
decisions.note: This key is intentionally temporary and should be removed when the scale decision is settled.

decisions.question: Which world structure should Deglyph use for slice 4?
decisions.answer: Use one large world coordinate space; later add streaming so the whole world is not loaded in one shot.
decisions.because: A single coordinate space is the chosen direction for leaving one screen and returning without making the world feel assembled from panels, while streaming is deliberately deferred until the larger-world probe proves the experience.
decisions.revisit_if: The larger-world probe shows that one coordinate space cannot support authored continuity, towns, dungeons, or player-made places without unacceptable loading or authoring costs.
decisions.note: one large field, but later we will add streaming so that we dont load it all in one shot
decisions.alternatives: A graph of screen-sized places with declared adjacency; chunks resolved from a field on demand; or a hybrid of streamed regions and separately authored places

questions.question: Which default cell scale makes the fullscreen world comfortable to read while preserving enough visible context for navigation?
questions.blocks: Choosing the final view distance and binding the declared view scale tunables.
options: Use a smaller cell scale so more of the world is visible
Use a larger cell scale so individual compositions read more clearly

direction.heading: Maps will be authored through a shared in-game editor
direction.accommodate: The persisted map shape must be readable and writable by the runtime editor used by developers and the community, with room for layered cell placement plus future triggers, collision, walkability, and edit-authority metadata.
direction.not_yet: Do not build the editor, ownership enforcement, layers, triggers, collision, or walkability in this slice.

direction.heading: Cells will grow into reusable visual compositions
direction.accommodate: The map representation must leave room for reusable grouped shapes such as items and trees, with future primitive rotation, axis flipping, and multiple shape types without making today's two-shape map ambiguous.
direction.not_yet: Use only empty and filled-square shapes now; do not build stamps, item variants, rotation, flipping, or the larger primitive vocabulary.
